newsitem.title: USA: Applebee's sees little Apple South impact.
newsitem.headline: Applebee's sees little Apple South impact.

text.p: Applebee's International Inc said Wednesday it does not expect to see a significant impact on its results from problems at Apple South Inc, its largest franchiser.
Apple South said Tuesday its earnings would be below analysts' estimates due to a management turnover and a sluggish restaurant environment.
"It should not significantly impact our results," Applebee's chief financial officer George Shadid said in an interview with Reuters.
"We do not think the things they have encountered in their system are really indicative or predictive on Applebee's as a concept," Shadid said.
In a news release, Apple South noted management turnover issues at its Applebee's division were a factor in lowering the companies earnings view.
Apple South, which operates 218 Applebee's Neighborhood Grill and Bar restaurants, said it will cut its development schedule to 45 from 48 for the rest of 1996 and 34 from 52 for 1997.
Lost royalties and franchise fees could have an impact on Applebee's 1996 and 1997 earnings, Shadid said, but stressed that the impact should be small.
"We think it's a few pennies," Shadid said. "It's not a major issue."
The First Call mean estimate for 1997 earnings is $1.55 a share.
Applebee's stock plunged 3-21/32 to 27-1/4 on Nasdaq Wednesday, a move some analysts did not think was warranted.

"I think it's important to decouple what happened at Apple South from Applebee's in terms of business fundamentals," Allan Hickok, analyst at Piper Jaffray, said in an interview. He said when Apple South acquired the Applebee's franchises, it had large turnover and had to raid the rest of its system to put management in the Applebee's restaurants.
Apple South fell 7-7/8 to 13 on Nasdaq wednesday.
